S001@7611-7692.words: do programmes meant to improve education for children and young people with disabilities work
S001@7611-7692.reason: A low-confidence rating on nearly all studies bears on how far the evidence shows that disability education programmes work, so a reader needs it to weigh the answer.

S001@7900-8058.reason: The judgement describes why disabled children fall behind, which is background on the education gap (explicitly out of scope), not evidence on whether any intervention works or which kind works best.

S001@8059-8153.reason: The judgement concerns equalising health outcomes, which the scope explicitly excludes as non-educational, so it does not bear on whether education programmes for disabled children work.

S001@8154-8406.reason: The judgement recommends a twin-track approach, combining disability-specific support with inclusion in mainstream activities through teacher skills and classroom accessibility, which bears directly on which programme types work best.

S001@8407-8703.reason: The judgement says most reviewed interventions targeted individual children rather than system- or school-level mainstreaming, which limits what the evidence can show about which programme types (e.g., inclusive versus individual-focused) work best.

S001@8704-8859.reason: The judgement says evaluation should focus on interventions that target the individual's broader environment as well as the individual, which bears on which programme types work best and on how much evidence exists for each.
